title: Spring gate switchyard
summary: A low-friction puck slides inside a U-shaped pen of bouncy rails that is open toward the right arm, and a spring-loaded swinging gate stands inside the pen. The left Panda has a bare gripper. It must take hold of the gate with both fingers and swing it open one way. The right Panda's paddle must then hit the puck so that it travels deep into the pen. While the puck runs round, the left hand, still gripping, must swing the gate the other way: at the moment the puck hits the upper (+y) rail, the gate must be at that opposite angle. The right paddle then intercepts the puck. Finally the puck must cross a goal line in front of a backstop on the right arm's side while the gate is still deflected well away from its rest position and the paddle is not touching the puck.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). It has no tool and uses the stock Panda parallel gripper: two fingers with a total opening of up to 0.08 m, fully open (0.04 m per finger) at reset. Its tool frame, reported as `panda-0_tool_pose`, is the gripper TCP between the fingertips. At the start the TCP is at (0.04, -0.10, 0.16), pointing straight down (quaternion (0, 1, 0, 0)), with the fingers closing along world y. panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). It carries a flat rigid paddle, 0.10 m long (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.05 m), 0.05 m tall and 12 mm thick, on a rigid adapter on its back (tool -x) side. The tool frame is the paddle centre, with x normal to its faces, y along its length and z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m behind the paddle centre and 0.04 m above it. Paddle start: centre (0.30, -0.08, 0.045), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg, faces normal to world x); its lower edge is then 0.020 m above the table. Role labels in every phase: panda-0 gate_operator, panda-1 preparing_striker.
scene: An orange square puck (44 mm x 44 mm, 24 mm tall) slides on the table with very little friction. At t = 0 it is already moving toward the right arm. Three fixed, very bouncy orange rails, 60 mm tall, form a U-shaped pen open toward the right arm. The far rail is on the left arm's side, and two long side rails run along it: the upper rail on the +y side and the lower rail on the -y side. Inside the pen stands a swinging gate: an amber leaf 0.13 m long, 55 mm tall and 12 mm thick that turns about a vertical hinge at one end. Its lower edge is just above the table, so the puck cannot pass beneath it. A raised orange-red handle block (32 x 24 x 24 mm) sits on the leaf's free end. A weak torsional spring pulls the gate back toward its rest orientation, in which the leaf runs along the world y axis, and the hinge is nearly frictionless. A short, non-bouncy backstop wall (0.14 m wide, 60 mm tall) stands outside the pen, beyond the goal line on the right arm's side. Only the puck moves at the start; the gate moves when pushed and springs back when let go. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Puck: box 0.044 x 0.044 x 0.024 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, friction 0.01, restitution 0.65. At reset it is placed at (0.20, -0.06 + u, 0.0125), with u drawn uniformly in [-0.008, 0.008] m, and velocity (+`incoming_speed`, 0, 0) = (0.35, 0, 0) m/s. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.015. Gate (fixture `gate`; hinge state reported as `gate_state` = [q, dq/dt]): fixed hinge at (0.10, 0.05, 0.015), revolute about world +z, limits [-1.5, 1.5] rad, joint friction 0.0002, joint damping 0.001. A spring drive pulls it toward q = 0 with stiffness 0.015 N m/rad, damping 0.005 N m s/rad and a torque limit of 0.25 N m. At q = 0 the leaf (12 mm x 0.13 m x 55 mm, friction 0.2, restitution 0.35) runs from the hinge toward -y. It spans y from 0.05 to -0.08 at x = 0.10, and z from 0.015 to 0.07. The handle block is centred at (0.10, -0.08, 0.085). Positive q swings the free end toward +x (counter-clockwise seen from above). Reset: q = 0, at rest. Rails (static, friction 0.3, restitution 0.75, 60 mm tall): far_rail is 0.016 x 0.36 m, centred at (-0.12, 0.05, 0.03), spanning y from -0.13 to 0.23. upper_rail is 0.40 x 0.016 m, centred at (0.08, 0.23, 0.03), spanning x from -0.12 to 0.28. lower_rail is 0.40 x 0.016 m, centred at (0.08, -0.15, 0.03). backstop (static, restitution 0.05): 0.02 x 0.14 x 0.06 m, centred at (0.48, 0.15, 0.03). Paddle: `tool_half` = 0.05, `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. The table top spans x in [-0.54, 0.70] and y in [-0.48, 0.48]. Horizon `horizon` = 35 s. The only random draw is u, made at reset.

phases.name: left_gate_open
phases.text: Two things hold at the same moment. Both fingers of panda-0's gripper (the left finger and the right finger, each counting together with its pad) are in contact with the gate's swinging part (leaf or handle). And the gate angle q exceeds 0.5 rad. q is 0 at the spring's rest orientation and positive when the free end swings toward +x (counter-clockwise seen from above).

phases.name: right_loop_shot
phases.text: The puck touches the right paddle at some moment during this phase; touches before this phase do not count. After that, the puck's centre is at world x < -0.05 while the puck does not touch the right paddle.

phases.name: gate_reconfiguration
phases.text: At one and the same moment, three things hold. Both left fingers touch the gate's swinging part. The gate angle q is below -0.35 rad. And the puck is in contact with the upper rail (the rail on the +y side of the pen).

phases.name: return_interception
phases.text: The puck touches the right paddle.

phases.name: final_gate_shot
phases.text: The puck's centre crosses x = 0.43 moving in +x, with |y - 0.15| < 0.055 m. Moving in +x means x was <= 0.43 on the previous physics step and is > 0.43 now. At that moment the puck must not touch the right paddle, and the gate must be deflected by more than 0.3 rad either way (|q| > 0.3); no grip is required. This completes the task.

contact_rules: The gripper fingers and finger pads of either arm may touch the puck and the gate's swinging part (leaf and handle). They must not touch the gate's base, the rails, the backstop, the table or the robot pedestals. The right paddle, including its adapter, may touch only the puck, not the gate, rails, backstop or table. No other robot part, such as the hand or the arm links, may touch anything. The two arms and the paddle must never touch each other, and the paddle must not touch its own arm.
world_goals_fixed: Goal line for the puck's centre: x = 0.43, crossed in +x with |y - 0.15| < 0.055 m. It is announced at reset as `goal_goal` = (0.43, 0.15, 0.012). Loop line: the puck's centre must get to x < -0.05. Gate angle thresholds: q > 0.5 rad, q < -0.35 rad and |q| > 0.3 rad.
difficulty_note: The left hand must keep a two-finger hold on a light, spring-loaded gate and swing it from one side to the other in time with a fast, bouncing puck. The swing must reach the opposite angle exactly when the puck hits the upper rail. Meanwhile the right paddle must time two separate contacts, and the final crossing still needs the gate held well open.
standard_notes: The puck is already sliding toward the right paddle at t = 0, before the gate can have been opened. A paddle contact before the gate is open does not count as the first shot. The gate springs back toward its rest orientation whenever it is let go.
